product.name: Magic BG Remover
product.tagline: instant cutouts, right in the tab
product.summary: Removes image backgrounds entirely in the browser. The image never leaves the tab.

press.short: Magic BG Remover is a free AI background remover that runs entirely in the browser — the image never leaves the tab.
press.long: Magic BG Remover strips backgrounds from images using a model that runs inside the browser tab, so the image is loaded, processed and downloaded without ever leaving the device. It installs as a PWA and works offline after first load.
press.naming: Written "Magic BG Remover" — "BG" always uppercase, never "Magic Background Remover".

sections.heading: Three ways to cut a background out

items.title: On-device AI segmentation
items.body: The model runs in the tab, on your GPU, and handles photos and complex edges.

items.title: Flood-fill and transparent-trim
items.body: For the easy cases: click a solid ground away, or trim what is already separated.

items.title: Installs and works offline
items.body: A PWA that keeps working with no connection after the first visit.

items.title: Exports worth keeping
items.body: OxiPNG (lossless), WebP and AVIF, with a live size preview before you commit.

items.title: Nothing upstream
items.body: No uploads, no accounts, no server. The tab is the whole pipeline.

sections.heading: From photo to cutout
sections.intro: Three paths in, one comparison, one export.

steps.title: Drop or paste the image
steps.body: It opens in the tab. Nothing is sent anywhere — check the network tab if you like.

steps.title: Pick the path that fits
steps.body: AI segmentation for photos, flood-fill for solid grounds, transparent-trim for what is already separated.

steps.title: Compare before and after
steps.body: The slider shows the two side by side, with studio background colours if you want a ground instead of transparency.

steps.title: Export at the size you choose
steps.body: OxiPNG for lossless, WebP or AVIF for weight — with the size preview live as you switch.

items.a: No. The model runs in the tab on your device; there is no server to upload to. The app keeps working with the network off.

Modern Chromium, Firefox and Safari — anything that runs WebGPU/WASM inference. The installable PWA works offline after the first load.
A lossless PNG optimizer. The export runs it for you, so a transparent cutout comes out as small as it can be without losing a pixel.
